purpose: E7 self-authored ambiguity subset: ambiguous questions with two checked readings and a frozen intended meaning, plus clear negatives. Written before any model run on these items.

items.question: What is the name of the heaviest hero?

readings.meaning: the hero's superhero name
readings.sql: SELECT superhero_name FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg IS NOT NULL ORDER BY weight_kg DESC LIMIT 1

readings.meaning: the hero's full real name
readings.sql: SELECT full_name FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg IS NOT NULL ORDER BY weight_kg DESC LIMIT 1

items.reply: I mean the superhero name the character is known by, not the real full name.

items.question: How many heroes have no height recorded?

readings.meaning: height is NULL
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero WHERE height_cm IS NULL

readings.meaning: height is NULL or 0
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero WHERE height_cm IS NULL OR height_cm = 0

items.reply: Count heroes whose height is missing, including heights stored as 0.

items.question: What is the average weight of Marvel Comics heroes?

readings.meaning: average over all Marvel heroes including weights of 0
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(s.weight_kg) FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'

readings.meaning: average excluding missing or zero weights
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(s.weight_kg) FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND s.weight_kg > 0

items.reply: Ignore heroes whose weight is missing or recorded as 0.

items.question: Which hero has the most superpowers?

readings.meaning: the hero name only
readings.sql: SELECT s.superhero_name FROM superhero s JOIN hero_power hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id GROUP BY s.superhero_name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

readings.meaning: the hero name and the number of powers
readings.sql: SELECT s.superhero_name, COUNT(*) FROM superhero s JOIN hero_power hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id GROUP BY s.superhero_name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

items.reply: Give the hero's name together with how many superpowers they have.

items.question: What percentage of heroes are female?

readings.meaning: female heroes out of all heroes
readings.sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM superhero s JOIN gender g ON g.id = s.gender_id

readings.meaning: female heroes out of heroes with a known gender
readings.sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM superhero s JOIN gender g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender <> 'N/A'

items.reply: Out of all heroes in the data, whatever their recorded gender.

items.question: Which race has the most heroes?

readings.meaning: including the unknown race placeholder '-'
readings.sql: SELECT r.race FROM superhero s JOIN race r ON r.id = s.race_id GROUP BY r.race ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

readings.meaning: among real race values, excluding '-'
readings.sql: SELECT r.race FROM superhero s JOIN race r ON r.id = s.race_id WHERE r.race <> '-' GROUP BY r.race ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

items.reply: Only real races; skip heroes whose race is unknown or shown as '-'.

items.question: Who has won the most races?

readings.meaning: the driver with the most race wins
readings.sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid WHERE r.position = 1 GROUP BY d.driverid, d.forename, d.surname ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

readings.meaning: the constructor with the most race wins
readings.sql: SELECT c.name FROM results r JOIN constructors c ON c.constructorid = r.constructorid WHERE r.position = 1 GROUP BY c.constructorid, c.name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

items.reply: I mean the driver with the most wins; give their first and last name.

items.question: How many races did Lewis Hamilton finish?

readings.meaning: races with a classified finishing position
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid WHERE d.forename = 'Lewis' AND d.surname = 'Hamilton' AND r.position IS NOT NULL

readings.meaning: races with status exactly 'Finished' (lead lap)
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid JOIN status st ON st.statusid = r.statusid WHERE d.forename = 'Lewis' AND d.surname = 'Hamilton' AND st.status = 'Finished'

items.reply: Count every race where he has a classified finishing position, even if he was lapped.

items.question: What is Lewis Hamilton's average finishing position?

readings.meaning: average official position over classified finishes
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(r.position) FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid WHERE d.forename = 'Lewis' AND d.surname = 'Hamilton' AND r.position IS NOT NULL

readings.meaning: average position order over every race entered
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(r.positionorder) FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid WHERE d.forename = 'Lewis' AND d.surname = 'Hamilton'

items.reply: Average his official finishing position, only over races where he was classified.

items.question: Which circuits are in Italy?

readings.meaning: circuit names
readings.sql: SELECT name FROM circuits WHERE country = 'Italy'

readings.meaning: circuit names and their locations
readings.sql: SELECT name, location FROM circuits WHERE country = 'Italy'

items.reply: List each circuit's name together with the town it is in.

items.question: Who won the 2017 Monaco Grand Prix?

readings.meaning: the winning driver's first and last name
readings.sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceid = r.raceid JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid WHERE ra.year = 2017 AND ra.name = 'Monaco Grand Prix' AND r.position = 1

readings.meaning: the winning driver and constructor
readings.sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, c.name FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceid = r.raceid JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid JOIN constructors c ON c.constructorid = r.constructorid WHERE ra.year = 2017 AND ra.name = 'Monaco Grand Prix' AND r.position = 1

items.reply: Just the winning driver's first and last name.

items.question: How many points per race did Sebastian Vettel average?

readings.meaning: average over every race he entered
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(r.points) FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid WHERE d.forename = 'Sebastian' AND d.surname = 'Vettel'

readings.meaning: average over races where he scored
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(r.points) FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = r.driverid WHERE d.forename = 'Sebastian' AND d.surname = 'Vettel' AND r.points > 0

items.reply: Average over every race he entered, including races with zero points.

items.question: Which country has hosted the most races?

readings.meaning: the country with the most races held
readings.sql: SELECT c.country FROM races ra JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitid = ra.circuitid GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

readings.meaning: the country with the most circuits
readings.sql: SELECT country FROM circuits GROUP BY country ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

items.reply: Count the races held, using the country of each race's circuit.

items.question: What is the average budget per event?

readings.meaning: average of individual budget lines
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(amount) FROM budget

readings.meaning: average of each event's total budget
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(total) FROM (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(amount) AS total FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) AS per_event

items.reply: Add up each event's budget lines first, then average those event totals.

items.question: How many members does the club have?

readings.meaning: everyone in the member table
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM member

readings.meaning: only people whose position is Member
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM member WHERE position = 'Member'

items.reply: Only people whose position is 'Member', not officers or inactive people.

items.question: Which event had the largest budget?

readings.meaning: the event name
readings.sql: SELECT e.event_name FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name ORDER BY SUM(b.amount) DESC LIMIT 1

readings.meaning: the event name and its total budget
readings.sql: SELECT e.event_name, SUM(b.amount) FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name ORDER BY SUM(b.amount) DESC LIMIT 1

items.reply: Give the event name and its total budgeted amount.

items.question: How many events were held in 2019?

readings.meaning: all events dated in 2019
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event WHERE event_date LIKE '2019%'

readings.meaning: 2019 events that already took place (status Closed)
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event WHERE event_date LIKE '2019%' AND status = 'Closed'

items.reply: Only events that actually took place, meaning their status is Closed.

items.question: What is the name of the club president?

readings.meaning: first name only
readings.sql: SELECT first_name FROM member WHERE position = 'President'

readings.meaning: first and last name
readings.sql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM member WHERE position = 'President'

items.reply: Their first and last name.

items.question: What is the average cost of an expense?

readings.meaning: over all expenses
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(cost) FROM expense

readings.meaning: over approved expenses only
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(cost) FROM expense WHERE approved = 'true'

items.reply: Only expenses that were approved.

items.question: How many schools are in Fresno?

readings.meaning: schools in Fresno county
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schools WHERE county = 'Fresno'

readings.meaning: schools in the city of Fresno
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schools WHERE city = 'Fresno'

items.reply: Schools located in the city of Fresno, not the whole county.

items.question: How many schools are there in Alameda county?

readings.meaning: every school record, including closed or merged
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schools WHERE county = 'Alameda'

readings.meaning: only active schools
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schools WHERE county = 'Alameda' AND statustype = 'Active'

items.reply: Only schools that are currently active, not closed or merged ones.

items.question: What is the average SAT math score in Los Angeles county?

readings.meaning: simple average of school averages
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(avgscrmath) FROM satscores WHERE cname = 'Los Angeles'

readings.meaning: average weighted by number of test takers
readings.sql: SELECT SUM(avgscrmath * numtsttakr) * 1.0 / SUM(numtsttakr) FROM satscores WHERE cname = 'Los Angeles' AND avgscrmath IS NOT NULL

items.reply: A simple average of each school's average math score.

items.question: Which school has the highest free meal count?

readings.meaning: the school name
readings.sql: SELECT "School Name" FROM frpm WHERE "Free Meal Count (K-12)" IS NOT NULL ORDER BY "Free Meal Count (K-12)" DESC LIMIT 1

readings.meaning: the school name and its count
readings.sql: SELECT "School Name", "Free Meal Count (K-12)" FROM frpm WHERE "Free Meal Count (K-12)" IS NOT NULL ORDER BY "Free Meal Count (K-12)" DESC LIMIT 1

items.reply: Only the school's name.

items.question: How many charter schools are there?

readings.meaning: charter flag in the school directory
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schools WHERE charter = 1

readings.meaning: charter flag in the free-meal (FRPM) table
readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM frpm WHERE "Charter School (Y/N)" = 1

items.reply: Use the school directory's charter flag, across all schools listed there.

items.question: What is the average number of SAT test takers in Fresno county?

readings.meaning: over every SAT row, including district summary rows
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(numtsttakr) FROM satscores WHERE cname = 'Fresno'

readings.meaning: over individual school rows only
readings.sql: SELECT AVG(numtsttakr) FROM satscores WHERE cname = 'Fresno' AND rtype = 'S'

items.reply: Average over individual schools only, not district summary rows.

items.question: In which year was the earliest race in the data held?
items.gold_sql: SELECT MIN(year) FROM races

items.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '='
